No sample-specific phase/unit cell coordinates in scoped main or SI pp.1–2.

productContexts.label: An-exposed QD solution
notes: This is an optical ligand-exposure series on the 2.9 nm core batch, not a separately measured size/morphology outcome.
Individual plotted ligand concentrations and surface coverages are unreported in scoped methods.
Figure 2 steady-state PL/PL0 uses 503 nm excitation (main printed 1044); this is an optical readout condition, not a growth condition.

productContexts.label: (Me)2N-An-exposed QD solution
notes: Separate 3.0 nm QD batch; growth adjustment and TEM panel not reported. Do not assign Figure 1B to this product.

SI Figure S2 calls the separate kinetics experiment 2.9 nm for each R-An; main Figure 2 assigns the dimethyl steady-state series to a separate 3.0 nm batch. Correspondence of those distinct datasets/batches is unresolved, so the captions are not asserted to contradict one another.
No graph edge to the 2.9 nm Figure 1 specimen or its TEM result.

Paper-wide purification, freshly distilled CHCl3 redispersion to 5.1×10^-7–6.0×10^-7 M and three-day N2 conditioning are represented as a shared method for this separate batch; its exact growth settings remain unknown.
Figure 2 steady-state PL/PL0 uses 503 nm excitation (main printed 1044); this is an optical readout condition, not a growth condition.

productContexts.label: Figure 6 group 1, one MeOH precipitation, 3.2 nm
notes: One arm of a single 3.2 nm synthetic batch split for a purification comparison.
No separately documented 3.2 nm growth charge, TEM micrograph or crystal phase.
Figure 6A is PL/PL0 optical response; Figure 6B is a schematic, not measured morphology.

productContexts.label: Figure 6 group 2, two MeOH precipitations, 3.2 nm
notes: The same source batch as group 1 receives one additional MeOH precipitation.
SI Figure S10 reports decreased free native ligands relative to group 1.
Figure 6 is not a 3.2 nm structure measurement; the full growth recipe is unavailable.

productContexts.label: Ten-batch 2.7–3.2 nm quantum-yield aggregate
notes: PL quantum-yield means and ± spreads are across ten 2.7–3.2 nm batches prepared like group 1 or group 2.
These values must not be assigned to the exact Figure 6 3.2 nm pair.

general_background.title: Injection and precursor supply
general_background.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
